items.label: f01-board-load-flow
items.front: Trace a BuildJira board load from browser to rendered columns.
items.back: Browser loads index.html/styles.css/app.js; app.js calls GET /api/projects; UI picks ATLAS or the first project; app.js calls GET /api/projects/{key}/board; BuildJiraStore.GetBoard maps in-memory entities to DTOs; the frontend renders metrics, columns, cards and the editor.

items.label: f03-senior-auth-questions
items.front: What does a senior check about auth in BuildJira?
items.back: Can a user access another project? Does every write check membership, role and ownership? Are authorization failures tested? Are audit events trustworthy? Is CORS limited to expected origins?

items.label: f02-first-tests-to-port
items.front: Tests were not ported in the .NET migration. Which integration tests does the doc ask for first, and with what tool?
items.back: WebApplicationFactory integration tests for /health, board load, validation failure, viewer permission denial, issue update, and audit creation.

items.prompt: The C# domain models IssueStatus etc. as enums. Why does the JSON serializer emit them as strings such as IN_PROGRESS?

choices.text: System.Text.Json cannot serialise enums as numbers at all
To keep the API contract familiar to the old frontend shape
The JSON data file must stay easy for humans to edit by hand
So that unknown enum values are accepted without validation

choices: System.Text.Json cannot serialise enums as numbers at all
To keep the API contract familiar to the old frontend shape
The JSON data file must stay easy for humans to edit by hand
So that unknown enum values are accepted without validation

items.explanation: JsonStringEnumConverter keeps the contract compatible with the TypeScript-era shape (IN_PROGRESS, PROJECT_MANAGER, AT_RISK).

items.prompt: Two BuildJira instances are pointed at the same JSON data file. What does the architecture doc say?

choices.text: The second instance refuses to start while the file is open
They are safe, because the store lock is shared through the file
They would race: each private lock only covers its own process
Writes merge, because each instance rewrites only its own changes

choices: The second instance refuses to start while the file is open
They are safe, because the store lock is shared through the file
They would race: each private lock only covers its own process
Writes merge, because each instance rewrites only its own changes

items.explanation: The singleton plus private lock makes local requests safer but is not horizontally scalable; production needs scoped services and database transactions.

items.prompt: GET /api/audit is restricted by role. Which actors may list audit events?

choices.text: Any role that can write issues, including engineers
Admins only
Admins and project managers only
Every seeded user, since read routes are public

choices: Any role that can write issues, including engineers
Admins only
Admins and project managers only
Every seeded user, since read routes are public

items.explanation: Audit listing allows ADMIN and PROJECT_MANAGER; issue create/update additionally allows ENGINEER; read routes are public inside the local app.

items.prompt: Why does Program.cs use minimal APIs and a singleton BuildJiraStore rather than MVC controllers and scoped services?

choices.text: MVC controllers cannot serve static files from wwwroot in the same ASP.NET Core process
Minimal APIs are required by JSON-file persistence, and controllers cannot use a singleton
They fit a small route surface and simple local state; route modules and scoped data access come later
Scoped services are not supported in ASP.NET Core unless Entity Framework is installed

choices: MVC controllers cannot serve static files from wwwroot in the same ASP.NET Core process
Minimal APIs are required by JSON-file persistence, and controllers cannot use a singleton
They fit a small route surface and simple local state; route modules and scoped data access come later
Scoped services are not supported in ASP.NET Core unless Entity Framework is installed

items.explanation: The tradeoff table lists minimal APIs and the singleton store as acceptable now, with endpoint groups and scoped data access as next steps.

items.prompt: A request to a mutating route sends no x-user-id header. Another sends an x-user-id that matches no user. What happens to each?

choices.text: The first acts as the first seeded user; the second gets UNAUTHENTICATED
The first gets UNAUTHENTICATED; the second acts as a guest viewer
Both act as the first seeded user
Both get UNAUTHENTICATED

choices: The first acts as the first seeded user; the second gets UNAUTHENTICATED
The first gets UNAUTHENTICATED; the second acts as a guest viewer
Both act as the first seeded user
Both get UNAUTHENTICATED

items.explanation: The default-actor fallback is a demo mechanism that also complicates no-auth testing; it is not real authentication.

items.prompt: What happens on disk for every successful write in the migrated app?

choices.text: Nothing until the process shuts down cleanly
Only the changed issue is appended to the JSON file
The full in-memory state is serialised back to the JSON file
The change is written to a SQLite journal and flushed later

choices: Nothing until the process shuts down cleanly
Only the changed issue is appended to the JSON file
The full in-memory state is serialised back to the JSON file
The change is written to a SQLite journal and flushed later

items.explanation: It mutates under a lock, appends audit events, then rewrites the whole state - fine for a learning app, not a production persistence strategy.

items.prompt: Which of these does the single BuildJira ASP.NET Core process NOT do?

choices.text: Run a separate Node/Vite dev server for the browser UI
Expose the /api endpoints and /health
Persist seeded and runtime data to a local JSON file
Serve static assets from wwwroot

choices: Run a separate Node/Vite dev server for the browser UI
Expose the /api endpoints and /health
Persist seeded and runtime data to a local JSON file
Serve static assets from wwwroot

items.explanation: One process serves static files, the API, health and JSON persistence; React and the Node/Vite toolchain were removed from runtime.

items.prompt: Audit events are appended to the same JSON state file as the data they describe. What is the stated future direction?

choices.text: A separate audit microservice called over HTTP after writes
A transactional audit or outbox table in a real database
Writing audit events to the console log only, not to storage
Dropping audit events once the integration tests are ported

choices: A separate audit microservice called over HTTP after writes
A transactional audit or outbox table in a real database
Writing audit events to the console log only, not to storage
Dropping audit events once the integration tests are ported

items.explanation: Keeping audit in the same file keeps behavior visible today; production needs it in the same transaction as the change.

items.prompt: In the PATCH /api/issues/{id} flow, what does BuildJiraStore.UpdateIssue do first?

choices.text: Append the issue.updated event to the audit list
Look up the issue and return 404 if it is missing
Check the actor's role, before the lock and lookup
Validate the supplied fields against the current issue

choices: Append the issue.updated event to the audit list
Look up the issue and return 404 if it is missing
Check the actor's role, before the lock and lookup
Validate the supplied fields against the current issue

items.explanation: Order: resolve actor from x-user-id, role check, validate and mutate, append audit event, serialise the full state, return the DTO.

items.prompt: Before swapping JSON persistence for a database, which step does the doc recommend first?

choices.text: Introduce an interface such as IBuildJiraStore
Rewrite the static frontend as a React app first
Delete the JSON file and reseed from the database
Move every endpoint into MVC controller classes

choices: Introduce an interface such as IBuildJiraStore
Rewrite the static frontend as a React app first
Delete the JSON file and reseed from the database
Move every endpoint into MVC controller classes

items.explanation: The suggested sequence: integration tests, extract endpoint groups, introduce the interface, move validation into validators, then EF Core migrations.

items.prompt: Which statement does the guide list among the things a junior might miss?

choices.text: Validation failures double as authorization failures
The x-user-id header is a secure identity once CORS is configured
The audit trail proves who performed each change
Shared request schemas protect API shapes but not database constraints

choices: Validation failures double as authorization failures
The x-user-id header is a secure identity once CORS is configured
The audit trail proves who performed each change
Shared request schemas protect API shapes but not database constraints

items.explanation: The three junior blind spots: validation is not authorization, x-user-id is not secure identity, shared schemas do not protect DB constraints.

items.prompt: An ENGINEER knows the id of an issue in a project they are not a member of. Can they update it?

choices.text: No: issue ids are random GUIDs that cannot be guessed
No: the role guard also checks project membership first
Yes: there is no project-membership check, only role guards
Only if they also send the matching project key header

choices: No: issue ids are random GUIDs that cannot be guessed
No: the role guard also checks project membership first
Yes: there is no project-membership check, only role guards
Only if they also send the matching project key header

items.explanation: Validation is not authorization, and a role check is not an ownership check; the production design needs resource-level checks.
